items.title: A quasi-experimental study of abortion rates following gestational age limit changes in Japan
items.author: Naho Morisaki
items.content: Using a quasi-experimental approach to national data from 1989 to 1994 in Japan, Yanagawa et al. find that a gestational limit change was associated with a shift to earlier abortions just below the new limit.

items.title: Genetic similarity between partners has intensified throughout the 20th century
items.content: We developed a method that detects the genetic footprint of partner choice without requiring the input of partners’ genotypes. Instead, it reconstructs maternal and paternal genomes within a single individual, capturing half of each parental genome. Applied to nearly half a million people in the UK and Estonia, our method reveals partner similarity that has intensified for height and educational attainment over the past six decades.

items.title: How speech plans become spoken sequences
items.content: Speaking requires the brain to rapidly convert planned speech into precisely ordered vocal movements. Intracranial recordings reveal a cascade of neural processes in which syllable-level plans in the prefrontal cortex are linked to phoneme sequences in the motor cortex, which enables fluent speech articulation.

items.title: Neural dynamics underlying minute-timescale persistent behaviour in the human brain
items.author: Ueli Rutishauser
items.content: Courellis et al. examine how neurons in the human medial frontal cortex and hippocampus persistently represent context.

items.title: Voluntary attention regulates acute immune responses in humans
items.author: Liron Rozenkrantz
items.content: Mizrachi et al. show that directing attention to bodily sensations, rather than away, promotes more regulated acute inflammatory responses in healthy volunteers, revealing sensory and vagal pathways linking mind and immune function.

items.title: An agenda for real-world fairness research to inform policy and organizations
items.author: Keyu Wu
items.content: In this Perspective, Fehr and Wu argue that applying fairness research to markets, organizations and public policy requires solving fundamental unresolved questions about how fairness concerns are activated, shaped and measured. They propose a research agenda to address these challenges.

items.title: Parental haplotype reconstruction in up to 440,209 UK and Estonian individuals reveals recent assortative mating dynamics
items.author: Zoltán Kutalik
items.content: Reconstructing parental haplotypes for up to 440,209 UK and Estonian Biobank participants, the authors estimate genetic assortative mating across 69 traits and find that assortment for height and education has intensified in recent generations.

items.title: Short- and long-term shifts in food purchasing behaviours and nutrition disparities in the USA during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
items.author: Mary R. L’Abbé
items.content: Using US household grocery data from 2017–2022, Hu et al. find that lockdowns temporarily shifted purchases towards less processed foods, while ultraprocessed food spending later rose above pre-pandemic levels.
